## 5-line summary

1. Five shifts of the `software_developer` actor produced **five authored-but-unapplied artifacts** under `docs/patches/` (001 `repository_commit` stage-all, 002 `update_task` profiles, plus README and evidence notes), all comment-logged on cards `e816cc41` / `a5f95606`, never applied.
2. Root cause is environmental: this checkout has **no shell tool, no `validate_file_patch`/`apply_file_patch`, and no `codx/junior/file_patch/` module**, so the only write primitive is a whole-file rewrite — unusable on 2018- and 3604-line modules (card `76d97f04`).
3. Two real defects were confirmed by tracing code: `repository_commit` without `paths` reaches `git add -A` (`git_engine.py:4185` → `:3183`) while the CISO gate reviewed only `git commit -m`; and `update_task` advertises `profiles` (`:3486`) but drops it before the metadata block (`:3216`, `:2615-2634`).
4. Both patches had self-inflicted **hunk-arithmetic errors** (002 wrong new-side counts; 001 a missing context line) that would have made `git apply` reject them — found and corrected in turns 5 and 6.
5. Structural blocker: tool rounds hit the profile's `effort.max_iterations` (10) every shift, and `project_locate`/`read_folder`/`project_map` time out at 120 s (card `d8534b12`), so work stays plan-only until DECISION D1 (`f8e10ad1`) funds the harness or the actor profile gets a `max_tool_rounds`/`continuations` bump.

## Profiles API & knowledge UI conventions

## REST conventions for profiles endpoints

- Identity lives in the URL: `/profiles/knowledge/{profile_name}` + `project_id` as a **query** param on every endpoint. Never put `project_id`/`profile_name` in a request body.
- Bodies only describe the resource (`file_name`, `content`, `title`, `overwrite`).
- `PUT` = upsert (create or replace); `DELETE` takes the resource name as a query param (no DELETE body).
- FastAPI dependencies: one `Depends` chain validates project + profile (404) and permissions (403); FastAPI caches them per request. Do not re-resolve settings inside each handler.
- Request models: `ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` + explicit `min_length`/`max_length` matching the tool limits (file name 500, content 200000, rule 4000 = `MAX_RULE_CHARS`).
- Storage `ValueError` → HTTP 400 with the message verbatim; do not string-sniff to build other codes.

## Profile knowledge UI

- `ProfileKnowledgePanel.vue` (rules/files tabs, budget bar, confirm modal) is mounted in `ProfileViewer.vue`; it reads `can_write` from the server and renders read-only with a lock hint otherwise.
- Rules are composed into `profile.content`, so any rule change must trigger a profile reload (panel emits `changed` → viewer emits `refresh`).

## WhatsApp / Channels board convention

All WhatsApp / external-channel work is tracked on board **Channels**, column **WhatsApp** (see `channels/whatsapp-bridge-architecture.md`).

Decisions already made (do not re-open):
- Official **WhatsApp Cloud API**, full duplex. The **Groups API is out of scope**: groups are created by the user in WhatsApp and codx-junior only stores group id/name + syncs messages.
- **Secrets live in global settings → `integrations[]`** (generic list, will also host Slack). Not env-var references, not in `.codx` project JSON, not in git.
- Identity: `CodxUser` carries a phone number (`wa_id`) and an `enabled` WhatsApp flag; a chat-level config lists which participants are synced.
- One group `Chat` ↔ one WhatsApp group/DM; mirrored messages tagged in `Message.meta_data["channel"]`.

## Kanban boards / sprints / task destinations

Kanban catalogue = `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (`{version, boards: {name: {id,title,description,type,parent_id,columns[],active,last_update}}, tags}`) and is read/written through `ChatManager.load_kanban` / `save_kanban`.

- A board name IS the storage folder (`.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/`) and is also stored in `Chat.board`; renaming must move the folder AND rewrite every task, deleting must not orphan tasks.
- A **sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`**; membership lives on the task (`Chat.sprints` holds sprint names). Deleting a sprint must clean `Chat.sprints` on tasks of other boards.
- Canonical task states come from `codx/junior/planning_manager.py` `STATUS_ORDER` — never hardcode a second list.
- Board/sprint/column CRUD lives in `codx.junior.tools.project_manager_tools` (`create_board`, `create_sprint`, `update_board`, `delete_board`, `create_column`, `delete_column`) and destination validation is shared via the public `validate_task_destination(chat_manager, board, column, sprints, status)`, used by `create_task` too. Tasks are always created through `TaskManager.create_task`.

## Identity: ids are canonical, names are labels

Every persisted element has an immutable `id` (UUID) and names/titles are only LABELS.

- Board/sprint: `board["id"]` in `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (a sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`).
- Column: `column["id"]` inside its board entry.
- Chat/task: `Chat.id` (also the file name suffix).
- Message: `Message.id`, mirrored with the legacy `doc_id` (`id` is canonical).
- References on a chat: `Chat.kanban_id` (board id), `Chat.column_id`, `Chat.sprint_ids`
  (source of truth for sprint membership; `Chat.sprints` keeps display names).
- Storage folder is NOT the name: each board/column carries an immutable `folder`
  (`Chat.board_folder` / `Chat.column_folder` cache it). Renaming must only change the
  title — never…

- A board name IS the storage folder (`.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/`) and is also stored in `Chat.board`; renaming must move the folder AND rewrite every task, deleting must not orphan tasks.
- A **sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`**; membership lives on the task (`Chat.sprints` holds sprint names). Deleting a sprint must clean `Chat.sprints` on tasks of other boards.
- Canonical task states come from `codx/junior/planning_manager.py` `STATUS_ORDER` — never hardcode a second list.
- Board/sprint/column CRUD lives in `codx.junior.tools.project_manager_tools` (`create_board`, `create_sprint`, `update_board`, `delete_board`, `create_column`, `delete_column`) and destination validation is shared via the public `validate_task_destination(chat_manager, board, column, sprints, status)`, used by `create_task` too. Tasks are always created through `TaskManager.create_task`.

## Identity: ids are canonical, names are labels

Every persisted element has an immutable `id` (UUID) and names/titles are only LABELS.

- Board/sprint: `board["id"]` in `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (a sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`).
- Column: `column["id"]` inside its board entry.
- Chat/task: `Chat.id` (also the file name suffix).
- Message: `Message.id`, mirrored with the legacy `doc_id` (`id` is canonical).
- References on a chat: `Chat.kanban_id` (board id), `Chat.column_id`, `Chat.sprint_ids`
  (source of truth for sprint membership; `Chat.sprints` keeps display names).
- Storage folder is NOT the name: each board/column carries an immutable `folder`
  (`Chat.board_folder` / `Chat.column_folder` cache it). Renaming must only change the
  title — never…

request.content:
# 001 — `repository_commit` must never stage everything

**Card:** `e816cc41` — Add a command-execution tool to the registry (scope-corrected to
`repository_stage` / `repository_commit`)
**Status:** fix authored, **not applied** (no patch/hunk tool in this checkout — see `76d97f04`)
**Patch:** [`001-repository-commit-no-stage-all.patch`](./001-repository-commit-no-stage-all.patch)

## The defect

`codx/junior/tools/repository_tools.py` documents this contract (lines 1395-1398):

> Without `paths` the commit contains what is already staged (`git commit -m`). With
> `paths` only those files are staged first and then committed, so changes nobody named
> are never swept into the commit.

The implementation did the opposite:

```python
1447|    stage_all = not requested          # no paths -> True
1448|    if stage_all:
1449|        command = f'git commit -m "{message}"'
```

`stage_all=True` is not cosmetic — it reaches the engine:

| Hop | Location | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| tool | `repository_tools.py:1468-1470` | `engine.commit_changes(stage_all=True)` |
| engine | `codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py:4185-4188` | `if stage_all: self._commit_all(...)` |
| engine | `codx/junior/engine/git_engine.py:3183` | `_commit_all` → **`git add -A`** |

Consequences, all reproduced statically:

1. `repository_commit(message="x")` with no paths runs `git add -A` and commits **every**
   dirty file in the tree — the sweep the card forbids.
2. The command handed to the CISO gate (`ciso/gate.py` `guard_command`) is
   `git commit -m "x"`, i.e. the gate reviews a **strict subset** of what actually runs.
   A path-less commit is therefore an unreviewed `git add -A`.
3. The report line is inverted too (`repository_tools.py:1487`): a path-less commit
   printed "the files given in `paths`".

`repository_stage` is clean: it requires explicit paths (≤ `MAX_STAGE_PATHS`), has no
stage-all switch and stages through `GitWorkspaceEngine.stage_files`
(`codx/junior/engine/git_workspace.py:209`).

## The fix

Stop deriving staging from the *absence* of paths. Staging is done explicitly by
`engine.stage_files(requested)` and the commit never stages on its own:

* `stage_all=False` unconditionally (`git_engine.py:4189-4193` then runs a plain
  `git commit -m` against the index, exactly what the docstring promises).
* The gate command is built from `requested`, so gate and execution always agree.
* `stage_all` disappears from the function; the JSON report exposes `staged_paths`.

Four hunks, 10 lines net. `stage_all` occurs only inside `repository_commit`
(verified: 5 occurrences, lines 1447/1448/1469/1487/1505), so the patch is self-contained.

## Apply

```bash
cd <repo root>
git apply --check docs/patches/001-repository-commit-no-stage-all.patch
git apply docs/patches/001-repository-commit-no-stage-all.patch
```

## Verify

```bash
# 1. no path-less add: this must stay empty
git diff docs/patches/001-repository-commit-no-stage-all.patch   # sanity: file exists, tracked

# 2. behaviour, with a dirty tree
#    a) repository_commit(message="chore: probe")  -> commits only already-staged files
#    b) repository_commit(message="chore: probe", paths=["README.md"])
#       -> stages README.md only; another dirty file stays dirty
```

Regression test to add alongside (none exists today — neither tool has a test):

* dirty tree with `a.txt` staged and `b.txt` dirty → `repository_commit(message=...)`
  must return `success` with `b.txt` **still modified** (`git status --porcelain`).

## Related cards

* `76d97f04` — actors cannot apply a 10-line change to a 2018-line file: `file_patch`
  is not reachable (`codx/junior/tools/file_patch_tools.py` and
  `codx/junior/api/file_patch.py` **do not exist in this checkout**), so this patch is
  the deliverable until a hunk editor is exposed.
* `f8e10ad1` (DECISION D1) — each of these shifts ends plan-only for the same reason.
* `4cce4b23`, `39a2d6a4` — both need the same git plumbing and are blocked on the same

# Patch 002 — `update_task` silently drops `profiles`

Card: `a5f95606-7c81-4e80-bffb-d152c8e86132` (IT team)
Patch: `docs/patches/002-update-task-profiles.patch`
Author: software_developer, shift 4 (2026-11-18)

## Symptom

`project_manager(action="update_task", chat_id=..., profiles=["software_developer"])`
reports `status: updated` but the task keeps its previous profiles. There is no
error and no warning: the argument is validated by the tool schema, accepted by
the dispatcher, and then thrown away one frame later.

## Evidence (verified against the working tree)

| Step | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py:3483-3491` | The schema **advertises** `profiles`: *"Profiles/roles for the task or the comment. Taken ONLY from this argument…"* |
| 2 | `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py:3208-3225` | The dispatcher forwards `board … tags, schedule, schedule_context` — **`profiles` is missing**, although it is in scope (`profiles` is passed to `_action_request_changes` at `:3237`) |
| 3 | `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py:2529-2546` | `_action_update_task` has **no `profiles` parameter** |
| 4 | `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py:2615-2634` | The metadata block maps status/board/column/priority/due_date/wake_at/progress/assignees/tags — **no `profiles` key** |
| 5 | `codx/junior/chat_manager.py:1242-1247` | `update_chat_metadata` applies `setattr(chat, key, value)` when `hasattr(chat, key)` — so a `profiles` key **would** persist with no engine change |
| 6 | `codx/junior/db.py:460` | `Chat.profiles: List[str] = Field(default=[])` — the attribute exists, `hasattr` is `True` |

Conclusion: the write path is complete and correct; only the two lines that carry
`profiles` from the dispatcher into `metadata` are absent. `create_task`
(`:2460-2520`) and the comment path (`_append_comment` → `_to_profiles`, `:393`,

## Symptom

never persisted.

| 1 | `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py:3483-3491` | Schema advertises `profiles` — *"Taken ONLY from this argument … On update it REPLACES the list"* was a promise without an implementation. |

| 6 | `…:393-404` | `_to_profiles(value)` is the correct normalizer: `None → []`, string → `[string]`, strips, de-duplicates and removes a leading `@` (names are re-emitted as `@name` mentions). Already used by `create_task`. |
